llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed local clipboard-history assistant, but it should be treated as sensitive because clipboard archives can contain private data.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose and capabilities fit together: it recalls locally archived macOS clipboard contents, including text, URLs, files, images, PDFs, OCR text, and raw exports. That is inherently sensitive but not hidden.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions mostly steer agents toward narrow recall/search/timeline commands and JSON parsing. Mutating actions such as restore, forget, purge, settings changes, and app control are documented, but should require clear user intent.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installation is disclosed through Homebrew or Cargo for the required clipmem binary. The included setup script performs health checks, not installation or destructive actions.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: A local SQLite archive, macOS pasteboard access, local OCR, and a background watcher are proportionate to clipboard recall. The update-check path is disclosed but introduces limited network behavior outside ordinary recall.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Persistent clipboard capture and archive retention are core to the product and are disclosed. Users should configure retention, ignored apps, OCR, and API-key filtering before relying on it.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with a local clipboard history database. Clipboard data often includes passwords, tokens, private URLs, files, and screenshots; review retention, ignored apps, OCR, and API-key filtering, and only export or delete items when you explicitly intend to.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] expected: Restore, delete, purge, settings, OCR, and storage commands are real side-effecting capabilities, but they are documented as clipboard-management operations rather than hidden or unrelated behavior.
[SDI-2] expected: App settings, launch-at-login, update-check, and quit commands are peripheral to recall but are disclosed as menu bar app management and scoped in the main skill to cases where the user asks.
[SDI-2] unexpected: OpenClaw and Hermes install/uninstall commands are integration-maintenance functions, not recall functions. The artifacts do not instruct automatic use or conceal these commands, so this is guidance-worthy rather than a hold.
[SQP-2] expected: Historical clipboard retrieval can expose secrets and private material. The skill discloses that it archives every clipboard state locally, though a stronger privacy warning would improve user understanding.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The live update-check is not needed for clipboard recall, but the command reference explicitly states that it performs a latest-release lookup.
[SQP-2] expected: Raw export to disk is necessary for image/PDF recovery and includes overwrite/symlink safeguards, but users should choose secure paths because exported files create another persistent copy.
